To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“In social tagging systems, users tend to create a hierarchy of tags by creating a taxonomy that is both a tree and a lattice, and the structure of this taxonomy can be used to improve search results.”

(1) a simple algorithm that converts a large corpus of user-generated tags into a hierarchical taxonomy can be used to organize a large collection of data in a collaborative tagging system; (2) this taxonomy is navigable by users of the system; (3) users are able to find the tags they need to annotate new objects; and (4) this algorithm is effective in these types, but not all, types of systems.

the collaborative creation of hierarchical taxonomies is an effective means to organize the information in social tagging systems and that the effectiveness is due to the emergence of a small set of tags that are highly correlated to the objects they annotate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether a large corpus of unstructured tags can be converted into a structured taxonomy of tags.
the question: How can we collaboratively construct a hierarchical taxonomy of tags that reflects the collective wisdom of a large community of users?
the creation of hierarchical taxonomies of tags from the bottom up, using the tags themselves as the primary source of information.

the algorithm we have developed is a simple but effective way to create hierarchical tag taxonomies that can be used to organize large corpora of tagged objects.
the algorithm works well in these systems because it is a simple and intuitive way for users to organize tags into a hierarchy.
this algorithm works well in tagging systems because the tags that are used in the system tend to be semantically related to one another.

we are proposing a method for collaborative hierarchical taxonomy creation, which is a new concept in the field of collaborative information organization.
collaborative tagging systems can provide a rich source of user-contributed metadata that can be used in the construction of navigable taxonomies.
we present a novel algorithm for the creation of a hierarchical taxonomy from a set of tags in a collaborative tagging system.

the algorithm is able to automatically discover a hierarchical taxonomy of tags that reflects the way in which people organize their thoughts about a given topic.

the tags used by users to annotate objects in tagging systems have the potential to form a useful and usable hierarchical taxonomy of tags, even when the tags are not explicitly organized into a hierarchy.
the tags in a collaborative tagging system can be used to automatically construct a hierarchical taxonomy that is highly relevant to the users of the tagging system.
